reader.requirement: At --std 85, each FD associates its file-name with its own file connector (an EXTERNAL FD in two programs with the same connector, a non-external FD a separate connector per program), and an FD whose file-name no SELECT names, or a SELECT with no FD, is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: passes DialectLevel as the connector's Edition; the connector-per-FD association is the same code

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|EditionContext|DialectBehavior in FileControlBinder.FileSection.cs#BindFileSection: the FD-to-FileModel association consults none (other edition tests there concern clause screening)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f17_02 covers two local FDs with separate connectors; not EXTERNAL connectors shared across programs, a contained program's same-named local FD, or the refusal of an FD/SELECT mismatch

probes.printed: INNER-WRITE-EF 00 (EXTERNAL EF opened by outer, written by inner); INNER-WRITE-LF 48 (inner local LF is its own unopened connector); EF read back OUT1, OUT2, OUT3, END 10
probes.expected: EXTERNAL FD shares the connector; local FD has its own

probes.printed: COBOL2636 file description entry 'F9' names a file that no file control entry specifies; COBOL2635 file 'F2' ... has no file description entry
probes.expected: an FD needs a file control entry and vice versa

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.3.2.4 GR1  (3.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: Correct behaviour. The refusals at --std 85 cite §2023 clauses (COBOL2636 cites §2023:13.4.5.3 SR1, COBOL2635 §2023:12.4.5.2 SR3) rather than the 1985 text; that is a diagnostic-wording matter outside this rule.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the connector association across nested scopes the reader did not try. src/r5glob.cob --std 85: an FD IS GLOBAL in the outer program; a contained program with no FD writes through it (IN1-GLOBAL-WRITE 00, record IG2 lands between OG1 and OG3 on read-back: G OG1, G IG2, G OG3, G END 10), so the inherited name reaches the outer connector; a second contained program declaring its own local FD of the same file-name gets its own connector (IN2-LOCAL-WRITE 48 into its own FS-L before its OPEN, FS-G untouched; then OPEN/WRITE/CLOSE 00 on r5local.dat, the global file's records unaffected). src/r5nonglob.cob: a non-GLOBAL outer FD referenced from a contained program is refused (COBOL1639 'FN' is not defined as a file; 'RN' is not defined), and a second FD of one file-name in one program is refused (COBOL4250). With the reader's EXTERNAL probe (shared connector) and FD/SELECT mismatch refusals, every way 1985 lets an FD name a connector is covered. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.3.2.4 GR1 the text is in GR1.
